To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A novel method was developed for the purification of M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP) from sheep.
we have developed a new method that allows us to isolate Mycobacterium paratuberculosis (Mpt) from the intestinal mucosae of sheep with Johnes' disease.

we developed a purification method that allowed the isolation of M. avium ssp. parat. from sheep with Johne’s disease, and that the DNA isolated from this M. avium paratuberculosis could be used for IS900 restriction fragment length polymorphic (RFLP)-analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterisation of M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis in sheep with Johne’s disease.

developing a method for purifying M. avium paratuberculosis for RFLP analysis from the intestinal mucosal scrapings of sheep with Johnes disease in Australia, in order to investigate the epidemiology of this disease.
the development of an epidemiological tool to determine the source of infection and the spread of Johne's Disease in sheep in Australia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method described here is suitable for the isolation and purification of M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis for the purpose of RFLP analysis from the intestinal mucosal tissues of sheep with John's disease in Australia.

the RFLP patterns of the M. avium ssp. paratuberuclosis isolates from the sheep studied in this paper are distinct from those of the M. paratuberculosus isolates obtained from cattle in the same study.

the purification of M. avium paratuberculosis for DNA isolation from the intestinal mucosal lesions of sheep with Johnes disease is a feasible procedure and that the RFLP pattern is consistent with that of M. avim paratuberculosis in New Zealand sheep.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
M. avium paratuberculosis is not easily isolated in large quantities from sheep with multibaccillary Johne's Disease in Australia.

M. avium paratuberculosis can be purified from intestinal mucosa of infected sheep, that this purification is sufficiently robust to enable RFLP analysis and that this method is suitable for epidemiological purposes in Australia.
M. avium paratuberculosis can be purified from the intestines of sheep with Johnes disease in Australia and that RFLP analysis is possible.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the RFLP pattern for M. avium ssp. paratubercolosis from sheep in Australia is different from that for M. av. paratuberculosi from cattle, and that this can be used to identify the source of infection in sheep with Johne’s disease.
the method of purification of M. avium ssp. paratuberuclosis described here can be applied in Australia to obtain sufficient DNA for RFLP studies of the epidemiology of the disease in sheep.
the purification method is robust, and that it can be applied to the analysis of M. avium subspecies paratuberculosis isolates from sheep and cattle.
